text_original: Van Persia den 3„' feb 1738 Batavia Aan zijn Edelheijd den Hoog Edelgroot Agtb: Heere den Heere Abraham Patras Gouverneur Generaal b'revens de welEdele Heeren Raden van Neds India Hoog Edel gestrenge Groot Agtb- Erntfeste manhafte wel wijse verresiende en seer Genereule Heeren Hoog Edele Gebiedende Heeren Het doodelyk Climaat deeser lugtstreek waar door den mensche in geduursame Elenden onderhouden werde buyten andere sorglykheeden nog zo veel niet wel des Begeerbegies mermet Tackje Chans gedaan be drijf in d EComp alhier sodanig te ladeeren ons als die alles gerings te onderdanen willende taxeeren zijn hoog Edele gestr. gr. Achtb. Heeren van grooten gewigt en niet onbeschryflyk lijden vermengd suppri neerende als regt en agtinge in een tijd waarinne na ppligte overweeginge den Coning met Eens gerustelijk mogen incommodeeren met onse klagten of men soude oogschynelyk, nog al mede ondergang of schade van den begeerbegie mogen vermoeden, so lange hy dat pouvoir over onsen alle Europeanen van zyn may. t behoud dog den spot en declinatie aan ons /schoon ongefundeerd / beweesen fundeeren d. teegenwoordige Persiaanse heeren opt geval der Engelse wegen hoen voortyds gedane vlugt en onversogte weederkeer, dan Europeanen zijn Europeanen verliet en zyn fatsoen den anderen ook en dus is geen andere oorsaake van ons lyden dan dat de britten hun scheepen met lles daar toe gerequireerd werd, verkogt hebbe en nog met alles, waarom moar spreeken geryven en Contirueeren telkens en grote schenkagies Van Persia den 22 february 1738 te doen tractementen nog apart. den Persiaan dog den begeerbegie wel het meest vermeend vast d' E Comp. kan Persiaan, gelyk van de mede Compe. titeuren gezien en g'oordeelt hebben, niet missen ook dat deselve hem niet gewassen is en derhalven ons submiteeren moeten alle strappazes en by langerduur onverdragelyker Tormentenschen dende na Eijge wille Keur het Jusgentum,
text_translated_detailed: From Persia, the 3rd February 1738, Batavia. To His Excellency the High and Noble, Most Esteemed Lord, the Lord Abraham Patras, Governor General, and likewise the Well-Honored Lords, Councillors of the Netherlands Indies. High and Noble, Strict, Great, Most Esteemed, Earnest, Mighty, Well-Wise, Foresighted, and Most Generous Lords, High and Noble, Commanding Lords. The deadly climate of this region of air, by which mankind is maintained in perpetual misery, and beyond other concerns, so much so that the conduct of the Beglerbegie Mermet Tackje Chan in the Company's affairs here is such that we, wishing to assess everything as insignificant to subordinates, are of the opinion that Your High Excellencies, Strict, Great, Most Esteemed Lords, are of great weight and not indescribable suffering, mixed with suppression, as is right and proper in a time when, after due consideration, the King may be troubled with ease by our complaints, or one might openly suspect damage or harm to the Beglerbegie, so long as he holds that power over all of us Europeans by his Majesty's will, yet the mockery and declination toward us, though unfounded, proves itself. The present Persian lords base themselves on the case of the English, as they formerly did with their flight and unsought return. For Europeans are Europeans, and they abandon their conduct to one another, and thus there is no other cause of our suffering than that the British have sold their ships with everything required for that, and continue to do so with all, why but speak and continue constantly with great gifts. From Persia, the 22nd February 1738, to conduct treatments separately. The Persian, though the Beglerbegie most of all, believes the E[ast India] Company can, as has been seen and judged by the other Company competitors, not do without, and also that the same is not equal to him, and therefore we must submit to all hardships and, with longer duration, increasingly unbearable torments, acting according to his own will and choice, the Jusgentum [uncertain: possibly a legal or administrative term],

text_translated_detailed:
From Persia, October 1, 1737, to Batavia. From His Excellency the highly esteemed and greatly respected, noble Lord Abraham Patras, Governor General, together with the well-esteemed greatly respected noble Lords, Councillors of the Dutch Indies, highly esteemed, stern, greatly respected, earnest, manly, wise, far-seeing, and most generous Lords. Highly esteemed, commanding, and gracious Lords.

Through the copy of Your Highly Esteemed Excellency's most reverenced letters dated the 58th of the past year, directed to the Lord Governor and Councillor at Gamron [Hormuz], we have perceived, to our particular delight and utmost obligation, the never sufficiently praiseworthy merciful righteousness with which Your Highly Esteemed Excellency has so generously deigned to favor us, lifting us from our oppressed and entirely dejected state. For in truth, and with all reverence spoken, Highly Esteemed Excellency, we had been driven by the continuation of harsh and violent persecutions from the Common Council to such a degree of despondency that despair had begun to gain the upper hand over our human weakness, and to such an extent that we no longer knew how to devise means to please or satisfy the Lord Governor and his further members, given that the passion there came through in such a way that we ourselves, with the prompt hearing together of the received orders, could also have done wrong, as if we were merely to be most sharply reprimanded and scrubbed according to the Lord Governor's pleasure through continued harsh treatment. Wherefore Your Highly Esteemed Excellency, through the Gamron succession in the letter written hereward, will be able to perceive clearly everywhere, namely how unjustly we have been treated by that College, or rather principally by the Lord Governor Koenad without intermission. We have read with all reverence your highly esteemed and truly most justified letter of concern, which was sent to Gamron [Bandar Abbas], regarding the fatal loss of money that was originally caused by the former Persian governor, the Mister Dames Hey, upon his departure from here, and subsequently by the broker Moultjend in accordance with his endless orders, dated as indicated, to the Company; and since your Excellency was pleased to have this matter remedied. Concerning this, through the unfortunate and until death downcast First Resident Gutchi, the lost accounting would be rendered, so shall the same, in obligated obedience according to his meager ability, assisted by the competent evidence documents at hand, endeavor to bring forth a fitting excuse, and beforehand approaching thereto with a sorrowful heart, he humbly submits himself before the threshold of your Excellency's feared tribunal, in which, beyond law and justice, healing and comfort for troubled minds is to be sought and obtained. Your Excellency's customary compassion would not be more powerfully demonstrated than by the undersigned bringing forth reasons of explanation; so would he greatly fear how, without difficulty, he could extricate himself from this dreadful course of confusion. Yet since grace is preferred over justice in the exercise of righteousness, I may well hope that my affairs will still be terminated most favorably through a necessary decision. From Persia, 3 October 1737. I beseech your Excellency, most esteemed and greatly honored, and always well-disposed gentlemen; be pleased, despite your Excellency's infinitely burdensome and troublesome concerns, to devote the effort and time to reading the attached documents hereto, and grant me, I beseech you, the permission to be briefer in this matter.

text_translated_detailed: that God may grant that he may remain honored until the end of his days, under the authority of their High Noble and Strict Excellencies, the most humble, most obedient, and most obligated servant, was signed G. Gutchi, in the margin. Bassora [Basra], the first of November, Persia dated the 18th of October 1727. I, Moeltjent, son of Ziekieser, acknowledge that this document was written by my own hand at Bassora. That the Honorable Mister George Gutchi, on the side that the business had some progress within the Company's lodge here, goods were sold, he repeatedly recommended to me to take care above all to exchange the received money and bring it into readiness so that if occasions should arise before the departure of the ship from the ships at Gamron [Hormuz], I could send it there on the said Commander's orders. I have given the Honorable Mister Gutchi assurance that the said money was always ready for his service so that I could send it at the first opportunity. The Honorable Mister Gutchi urged me not once or twice but well fifteen or twenty times to do so, and through my repeated word, my lord, set your mind at ease, the cash is ready whenever Your Excellency pleases. But to my sorrow, and having been forced to do so, I have used the Company's money from the sales and at my receipt some of the debts of Mister Heij to settle them, because the said gentleman assured me with his arrival at Gamron [Hormuz] to do his duty to pay off his outstanding debts to me at the first opportunity. But if it should come to pass and debt collectors should trouble me, I would settle it with the money coming into my cash so that I would still have some advantage from it, to make the interest fall more bearably. This is his saying at his request.

This is all that I am aware of, and God Almighty is my witness that all that I have here set forth is truth, containing it. For the said gentleman is deceased, and I am also a man who shall be subject to the same. Furthermore, I have received from Aleppo for the said gentleman's account 52 pieces of small list cloth or 1129 ells [modern equivalent: approximately 670 meters] by measurement. The said cloths have been inspected by me and charged to a sum of 62½ tomans [modern equivalent: Persian currency], having also requested me at the arrival of the said goods to give extra to Moeltjent, just as I also at receipt of those, Moeltjent has acknowledged and had called to come to receive them. text_translated_detailed: Persia, 4 February 1738. From Batavia. To His High Nobility, the High and Noble, strict and great Esteemed Lord Abraham Patras, Governor General, together with the well-born, great and esteemed Lords, Councilors of the Dutch Indies. High and Noble, strict, great and esteemed, most steadfast and wise men, most generous Lord, and herein high and noble, well-commanding Lords. (in margin:) in the ship under sail "Thuijs te Foreest" the 4th of February, year 1738. (and below) in the presence of us (signed:) C. Clement. Report made in all respect to the Esteemed Lord Carl Koenad [Carl Koenad:], Chief Merchant and Commander over the Company's important interests in the Kingdom of Persia, with the jurisdiction of that Esteemed Lord and Commander:— In accordance with the well-known highly esteemed order of our Lords Majors and your Esteemed further verbal instructions; the undersigned as Expressly appointed Members from the Judicial Council have on this day, together with the Fiscal of the Esteemed Caesar directorate Simon Clement, proceeded on board the ship "Thuijs te Foreest" [Thuijs te Foreest:] lying here at the roadstead under sail, in order to return to Malabar [Malabar:] and thence to Batavia [Batavia:], the same vessel. Having mustered the crew of the same according to custom and inspected them as best we could, we found therein no private goods, and the keel sixteen feet net with its forward and eighteen feet with its aft sternpost drawing deep. Thus hoping that we have fulfilled our duty, we remain with the obligatory respect (we remain) your Esteemed humble obedient and dutiful servants. (was signed:) J. de Wilt. J. W. Niepet. (in margin:) Gamron [Gamron:] the 4th of February, Anno 1738 (and below) in the presence of me (was signed) Pr. Clement.

text_original: Van Persia onder dato 31 xber 1737 Resolutien genomen in rade van politie Go Vrijdag den 7 februarij 1738. alle present, Exempt den E Willem Meester mits indispositie Door den EE heer Gesaghebber de vergaderinge belegt, en na dat een jder der presente Leden zitplaats genomen hadde 't gebruijkelijk gebed verright, mitsgaders ter ponderatie gegeven wesende, het vertrek van 't schip 't huijs te foreest na batavia op 3 Courant en dat ingevolge de getrokkene besluijten deser tafel in dato 5 en 24 december jongst leden de transporten en Jnstallatien &ca: der open gevalle bedieningen, als dan ook soude volgen door en aan sodanige g'Eligeerde personen als daar inne vermeld staan, zo is dan op de propositie van voors: zijn EE met eenparige stemmen goed gevonden, en besloten het een en ander na dies forme en inhoude te doen Effectueren mitsgaders uit dien hoofde aan den Coopman, en p=l negotie boekhouder d' heer Abraham van suchtelen, door Van Persia onder dato 31 xber 1737 den ondercoopman en debilen p=l pakhuijsmeester dE Willem Meester van 't Negotie Comptoir met dies aankleven te laten doen terwijl de g'eligeerde provisioneel fiscaal simon Clement van 't secretariaat en dispens al mede sal verrigten, aan zijn voorfangers den pl secrets van der Crap, en dispencier Anthonij Vink en de twe laast vermelte wederom Cok aan Steven pruijmelaar en Gerrit hendk Terre also dese tot eerste gesw: Clercq en soldij boekhouder verkoren en de bekleding deser bedieninge in derselver plaatse toevertrouwt zijn, terwijl in middens gesegde Crap als een wesentlijk lithvangen plaats vergund wierd, na dat alvorens door hem en gem: pruijmelaar, den tot hun lieden Emploij specterende eed voor gelesen en in handen van den eersten tekenaar deses Conform voorig gebruijkt afgelegt geworden was, als wanneer insgelyks in aanmerkinge quam de in de jongste besending
text_translated_detailed: From Persia dated 31 December 1737 Resolutions taken in the council of policy on Friday the 7th of February 1738, all present, except the Honourable Willem Meester due to indisposition. The meeting was convened by the Honourable Governor, and after each of the present members had taken their seat, the customary prayer was performed, and thereafter for consideration was given the departure of the ship the House to Foreest to Batavia on the 3rd current, and that in accordance with the decisions drawn up at this table dated 5 and 24 December last past, the transports and installations &ca: of the open vacant positions, as would then also follow through and to such elected persons as are mentioned therein, it was then upon the proposition of the aforesaid Honourable with unanimous votes deemed good and resolved to effect one and the other according to its form and content, and furthermore on that account to the merchant and p:l negotiation bookkeeper the Honourable Abraham van Suchtelen, through from Persia dated 31 December 1737 the under-merchant and deputy p:l warehouse master the Willem Meester of the Negotiation Office with its attendant matters to have done, while the elected provisional fiscal Simon Clement of the secretariat and dispensary shall also perform, to his predecessors the p:l secretary van der Crap, and dispenser Anthonij Vink and the two last mentioned again also to Steven Pruijmelaar and Gerrit Hendk Terre, as these were elected to first sworn clerk and salary bookkeeper and the filling of this position in their respective place is entrusted, while in the meantime the said Crap was granted an essential lithvangen [uncertain: possibly a specific administrative position] place, after that previously by him and the aforementioned Pruijmelaar, the oath pertaining to their employment was read aloud and deposited in the hands of the first signatory hereof in accordance with previous custom, as when likewise came into consideration the services rendered in the latest dispatch

text_translated_detailed: A Van and Governor of the Persian Directorate, with the jurisdiction thereof together with the council, most esteemed Lord and most esteemed Lords, the ship [uncertain: "opperdoes"] arrived here today, God willing, we the undersigned Members, from the respectable council of Justice of this Office, in the presence of the under-Merchant and provisional Fiscal Simon Clement, have proceeded on board of the same vessel, in order to inspect and examine that keel, according to the highly respected and most solemn orders given by their High Noble and strict Excellencies, the superior gentlemen in the fatherland, their High Excellencies in Batavia, and your Excellencies' further oral instructions, in order to ascertain whether any private goods were stowed therein. However, although we have conducted this inspection as carefully as possible and to the extent that was feasible, we could discover no private goods, the vessel drawing sixteen feet at the bow and eighteen feet at the stern. text_translated_detailed: The condition was that a broken batch of 198 pounds of cinnamon was such that it could not be made deliverable in any way, and was also sufficiently lacking in smell and taste. Therefore, as it is now understood, the entire quantity of that former aromatic bark is to be kept in readiness for shipment to Batavia, and although the recently brought turmeric, as well as ginger, are also not of much value, and it is plainly evident that with these sorts, according to the indication of the samples, their turnover can no longer be held up without difficulty, if one does not wish to see them become unsaleable, and therefore it has been judged more advisable to let the aforementioned cinnamon go to the merchant mentioned at 1½ to ƒ 12:12 per 6 pounds, and the ginger against 2:—:— to ƒ 17 per equal pound to help the man along. Furthermore, the brokers shall still be credited, and the account of expenses shall be charged to the merchant for what they have given to the planner of the two pieces of blue cloth, amounting to 6 to ƒ 2:11. Thus done, resolved, and arrested in the Dutch Company's office at Gamron, on the day, month, and year aforesaid (signed: C. Koenad, A. Mvr Suchtelen, W. Mleester, A. J. Vbercheijk). text_translated_detailed: On the 22nd of April 1738, signed by Mr. van der Crapt and the secretary of politics. In between, the Governor produced a draft compliment letter addressed to the Beglerbegie Mahamet Tachie of Persia, dated the 31st of December 1737. Regarding the progress made by him on the opposite shore, with which a member of the council confirmed it, and also resolved to demonstrate in these words how, in accordance with the decision drawn up on the 3rd of March last past, by Express commissioners the received tent for the aforementioned his Highness was inspected, and everything was found to be in the following manner. A report was made and delivered with all respect to the Esteemed and Honored Mr. Carel Koenad, chief merchant and Governor of this directorate, together with the Esteemed council. Commanding Sir and Esteemed Gentlemen. In obedience to your Esteemed respected orders, we undersigned, being expressly commissioned for this purpose, have betaken ourselves to the Company's ship lying here at the roadstead, the Opperdoes, and there in our presence had two chests opened, in which we found certain goods from Persia dated the 31st of December 1737, serving for a tent, as is specifically demonstrated below, namely. In chest No. 1: 5 long packages sewn and covered with white linen, yet not opened from the outside, dry and in good condition. 1 red package belonging to the underside of the tent, yet insofar as we have seen it, no infection or damage whatsoever was discovered. 5 painted poles with copper fittings without [uncertain: abbreviation] of wood. In chest No. 2: 50 pieces of iron tent nails, 90 hammers, 1 small basket with wooden blocks belonging to the tent. And since the aforementioned goods were dry and in good condition, we therefore had them stored again in such manner, and the chests properly secured and nailed. With which Esteemed Commanding Sir and Esteemed Gentlemen, we hope this our commission regarding Persia dated the 31st of December 1737 to have completed to the satisfaction of Your Esteemed

text_translated_detailed: generous lord and gentlemen. From Persia, dated 30 April 1738. Since we have been compelled to detain the bearer of the foregoing humble letter, the yacht D'Anthonia, here, and in its place, with that which was clarified for your Esteemed Honor, to dispatch the ship Opperdoes, it is still necessary to report for your valued information that regarding the required horses, we have been obliged to order the servants at Isfahan and Bandar Abbas on the 10th and 11th of this month to see to it, because the remaining charters, such as the aforementioned yacht and the Adriana, are too small to be able to transport a considerable portion of them, as we have already mentioned regarding one of them, yet orders have been given to both places that they must report to us how far the prospects for obtaining them have appeared, so that use may be made thereof when a good opportunity presents itself again. Concerning the Kerman sheep and kids, your Esteemed Honor's prudent proposal has been well considered, but has now also been thwarted by a terrible visitation of locusts which over 150 miles in circumference have consumed everything that the earth and trees provided for food in these ruined lands. From Persia, dated 30 April 1738. So that the owners of these animals are far away in Kerman to have them graze, and before they could be here, a good month and a half would pass, for which reason we are compelled to wait for a better opportunity, with the friendly request that you send us your positive wishes in writing regarding how many of each sort you require with the 2 attendants (if these can only be persuaded), for the rest, concerning the remaining goods, at the said time also regarding your Esteemed Honor's valued requisition, proper arrangements have been made, and we therefore live in hope that the fulfillment thereof shall come to good

To the Esteemed Sir Carel Roenad, chief merchant and commander over the Company's trade and commerce from Persia under date 30th April 1738, together with the Council of Gamron. Sir and particular good friends. Since our latest [letter] of the 12th August past, whose copy goes herewith, we have received through Pondicherry your Esteemed pleasant letters of the 20th July of this year with the accompanying attachments according to registers. We thank you for what was noted therein concerning the assafetida, ruinas, root, and likewise for the condition of certain inland matters, as well as for the sent 12 casks of rose water and 1 thereof with thyme seeds, which latter with 9 casks of the first our chief officers at Pondicherry from the French Governor at Pondicherry Monsieur du Mas have received, under the report from them that they will write regarding this, and since the said chief officers could see nothing of it, they are from Persia under date 30th April 1738 intending to write themselves regarding the still 3 missing casks of rose water. We cannot write off more from the salempouris mentioned by your request of the 30th September 1736 than 42 packages or 3360 pieces general bleached, which will remain unsent and set aside, having already 40 packages thereof been paid to Batavia, and we let come to you at the side of this the copies of our respectful letters, both to the Fatherland, to the Esteemed high honored gentlemen majors, as to the Esteemed high Indian government at Batavia sent under dates 27th February, 29th December of the previous [year], 24th June, 15th

At the Castle on the 29th of August 1737. [It is] agreed [and] was signed: S. Pruijngelaar & Clercq: G. Gersia. To the aforementioned.

We have received our letter of the 29th of the past month, of which the copy herewith goes [attached], [and we] have noted that the heads at Pondicherry from the French governor at Pondicherry, Monsieur Dumas, had not received more than [what came] from Persia under date 30 April 1738: cases of rose water and 1 [case] of garden seeds. And that they would write regarding the three cases of rose water that were missing, as has been done by them, and they have received in response that the aforementioned governor has sent them everything that had been unloaded by Captain Beaumont for that purpose at Pondicherry, but that His Excellency, on account of the shipment of the three cases of rose water to Bengal, for which Monsieur Beaumont with his ship L'Heureux had departed, would write, as Your Excellency can examine in more detail from the enclosed copy, translation, [and] letter from the aforementioned Monsieur Dumas. And since it could happen that through incorrect or careless handling of the matter the aforementioned 5 cases were transported elsewhere and unloaded differently, or that one could obtain no further information about them, we request that Your Excellency be pleased to send us such proofs as Your Excellency has at hand from Persia under date 30 April 1738, to the effect that Captain Beaumont took 12 cases of rose water and 1 [case] of garden seeds from Your Excellency for delivery to this Government, and that these were received for him or by Monsieur Philippine du Plantes according to his order. With which, after cordial greetings, we remain [your] obedient [servants]. E. Sir and by Cendere good Friends, [signed below] Your Excellency's willing Friends who [are] signed: J. Guillot, J. Mossel, B. Duijn, J. d. Fonseca, C. L. V. Drenteleen, W. de Jongh, J. Martensz, Rijnjak, L. Gravia,

text_translated_detailed: By the French ship: delegated and commissioned by Monsieur Vigoreux from Persia under date 30 April 1738. Signed: C. Koenrad, M. Suchtelen, W. Meester, A. J. Van Bercheijk, S. Clement, N.L. v.d.r. Crapaden, p.l. Secretary and Elegrand, / on the side / departs on 31 May 1738 / (accorded) / Surat. To the Honorable and esteemed Mister Pieter Laurens Phonsen, Director over the Company's considerable interests and wide commercial dealings in the kingdom of Guzerat, Hindustan, etc. Benevolent and advised, Honorable, esteemed, worthy, and very generous gentleman and friend, without our being held up with acknowledgment of what we have already transacted through our recent correspondence over the Malabar to your Honorable address on 31 January, we acknowledge receipt of your letter dated the last of December of the past year; in this regard the duplicate has arrived with us and along with a register of all such documents as were relevant thereto from Persia under date 30 April 1738, and have accompanied it. Thus it shall also be further reported how since that time news has arrived here that the small ship D'Anthonia, the scraggly and shameful to lose Beglerbeigi [Turkish provincial governor] Mahmed Tackie Khan would have been compliant, the same in the King's service to see it sail, and furthermore had already granted transport hither, which is not only to be wished but also still to be hoped for. The now arriving 2 chests, one with dragon vinegar and the other packed with the goods for the afternoon from Spahan received 15 pounds of turmeric seeds, 50 [units] of pistachios, shall be properly arranged and cared for, and at the same time found to be of the required quality and from that account shall partake in the pleasure of your Honorable address, from whom we most cordially request that this amount according to the invoice totaling ƒ 123, 16, 12 be brought to the benefit of this directorate. Persia under date 30 April 1738 to E. Underway.

text_translated_detailed: By the ship Opperdoes and the yacht Adriana, from Persia, under date 30 April 1738. To the Esteemed Mister Carel Koenad, chief merchant and governor, together with the council, at Gamron. In the most secure manner, [we greet you] very discreetly. With the arrival of the ships Stadwijk and Ritheim at this coast on the 12th of January and 11th of May last, we have been well provided with your Excellency's agreeable letters of the 38th of November of the past year and 6th of April of this year, together with such goods as have been shipped by your Excellency in the aforementioned vessel for this command, as well as for Ceylon and Coromandel, the latter of which we have had sent on as soon as possible, as your Excellency will be able to see from the accompanying papers from the aforementioned two governments and sent to us for further arrangement to your Excellency. From Persia, under date 30 April 1738. Whereas we thank your Excellency in a friendly manner for the good advice given in the letters regarding the Syrian Christians, with the earnest request that the two accompanying letters of the aforementioned Christians may be well arranged in the same manner through your Excellency's good care, as we further express our obligation to your Excellency for the friendly communication of the copies of their Batavian and Patriarchal advices, as well as for what your Excellency has been pleased to arrange for the service of this command, with the aforementioned keels, which here upon delivery has been better conducted than the Malabar pepper found by your Excellency. Regarding this shortfall in weight, we have, upon careful examination, been unable to discover any error, and therefore it must be attributed to another cause [unknown to us], all the more so since this cargo was already one year old at the time of shipment and consequently cannot be subject to any particular shrinkage. Nevertheless, we have resolved henceforth to pack the sample pepper in sailcloth instead of gunny sacks, to prevent, as much as is in our power, such excessive shrinkage. Furthermore, we hope that the two samples of Coarse linen cloth sent will have been better received by your Excellency than the alum received here, since no lovers of it have come forward. And regarding the asafetida, whose purchase your Excellency has discontinued, we request in your further letter that if the same can be obtained there at such a price as is stated in the requisition sent by us in the past year, we should see to it entirely. Furthermore, we hereby send you word from Persia, under date 30 April 1738, of Malabar turmeric, 1 candy [modern equivalent: approximately 500 pounds], and an equal amount of dried ginger, not suitable. We request that your Excellency be pleased to take a sample thereof, or whether one could not dispose of the same at Cochin with a reasonable advance to the greatest advantage, and in accordance with the express desire of our high superiors, in which case we would abundantly provide you with it. But regarding your Excellency's proposition, or the goods required of us, which are brought from the upper lands not without danger for our account and risk, by your Excellency, we can answer nothing other than that, being unable to judge the danger that might reside therein, and the fulfillment of our requisitions to your Excellency [rests] upon your own judgment and good consideration.

Furthermore, we hereby send you word from Persia, under date 30 April 1738, of Malabar turmeric, 1 candy approximately 500 pounds, and an equal amount of dried ginger, not suitable. We request that your Excellency be pleased to take a sample thereof, or whether one could not dispose of the same at Cochin with a reasonable advance to the greatest advantage, and in accordance with the express desire of our high superiors, in which case we would abundantly provide you with it. Erntfeste Manhafter wyse verresiende ende seer Genereusen heer en E Heeren Den fransen Capitain Mons. Vigoreug „ van dienst zijn aanbod, en de part op morgen ons geparticipeert hebbende, zal dien korten tusschen tijd niet toelaten, wijd lopig in desen t'ageren, maar eenelijk om te melden, dat de pest ziek, te nog al sterk blijft domineren, met vele menschen uijt de werelt te slepen, den heer Engelsch Consul Marten frensch, en zijn schrijver m=r kenni sijn daar onder gerekent, zo dat dat Engelsch huijs uitgestorven dog wederom in possessie genomen door enen m=r Dorril die ten dien eynde uijt bagdaad„ Van Persia onder dato 30 april 1738 is gearriveert en teffens om de affaires der natie hier waar te nemen, en der franse huij sen of dat van Mons=r La Rievierre, is mede door de dood ledig geraakt, en sijn dies bereddinge, benevens dien van den Overleden super Carga Mons=r Aumont, aan den bekenden docter du frisne geremitteerd, zo dat de meeste Europeesen in loco zijn gedesparoiseerd, wij zijn God dank nog onder de levende, dog zeer sober van gesonthijd en kragten voorzien, het thuijntjen voor desen gemeld, is voor als nog onse uijt vlugt, en is benevens de genade des hemels, ons eenig levens behoud, de stad is meest ledig de negotie staat stil, en wij bidden god maar om een genadige herstelling, en reddinge uijt de presente miserable gesteltenisse. Uijt een briefken per tranhi a boucher ontfangen, is ons tot bijsondre lief zijn gebleken, dat de negotie aldaar tamelijk wel slaagde, zo dat wij met blijdschap bemerkten onse vorige bekommernisse dient wegens nog ten besten is komen uijt
text_translated_detailed: From Persia under date 30 April 1738: To the Esteemed Heer Carel Koenad, chief merchant and governor of the Persian directorate and considerable official attached thereto, together with the council. Most earnest, manly, and very generous heer and esteemed gentlemen. The French Captain Monsieur Vigoreug's offer of service and the part communicated to us this morning will not allow us much time in between, to elaborate widely on this matter, but only to report that the plague sickness still remains quite strong, carrying many people from this world, the English Consul Marten French and his clerk Mr. Kenni are counted among them, so that the English house has been emptied but again taken into possession by a Mr. Dorril who for that purpose has arrived from Baghdad. From Persia under date 30 April 1738 and at the same time to look after the affairs of the nation here, and the French house or that of Monsieur La Rivière has likewise been left empty by death, and his effects, together with those of the deceased super cargo Monsieur Aumont, have been remitted to the well-known doctor du Frisne, so that most Europeans in loco have been dispersed, we are God be thanked still among the living, but very poorly provided with health and strength. The little garden mentioned before is for now our refuge, and is together with the grace of heaven our only means of survival. The city is mostly empty, business stands still, and we pray to God only for a merciful recovery and deliverance from the present miserable condition. From a small letter received per Tranhi à Boucher, it has been particularly pleasing to us that business there succeeded reasonably well, so that we noted with gladness that our previous concern regarding this matter has turned out for the best on the 20th of September of the year just past. From Persia under date 30 April 1738 we have sent the homeland packet, together with our accompanying letters, across the desert toward Aleppo, in such a way that the copy letter to the heer Consul van Liebergen your Excellency will be able to show, provided that we have hired for that purpose 2 express runners for 600 mammoths [uncertain: possibly a currency], in order to return as quickly as possible with the replies. The time being short and the first undersigned not being well disposed, we shall under your esteemed permission conclude this, with a heartfelt wish for all desirable welfare, blessing and prosperity upon the entry of this new year, and that the same may be opened to considerable progress in the Company's and your Excellencies' own interests, with which we then, most earnest, manly, and very generous heer and esteemed gentlemen, after recommendation of our persons in your Excellency's very esteemed favor with much respect, from Persia under date 30 April 1738 and submission remain, understood: your Excellency's entirely obedient, subordinate and obliged servants, was signed: G. Gutchi, C. de Maan, W. Claas, in margin: Bassoura on 19 January 1738, lower: the enclosed has come into our hands a few days ago from Aleppo, which we have the honor to present to you, the same together with the copy of that directed to us, herewith to enclose.

And as for the remaining merchandise, we are supplied with uncommon courage and likelihood of good success, especially concerning the fine linens, such as Cassas, malmolen and sollogesjes common sorts, provided that we were only supplied with them, the Syrian merchants have also shown inclination toward a partial purchase of coarse linens, but they cannot yet agree on the prices, yet we have had more and more traffic in recent days to conduct trade with us, so that we have reason to hope that God the Lord will graciously deign to heal the wounds caused by the plague again through a flourishing trade, may your Esteemed and Gentlemen take these our sincere reports into ripe consideration, and let the Noble Company profit happily from the probable impending trade, so we pray entirely from Persia under date 30

Upon which then, to profit from that gentleman's further advice, such a petition was brought into readiness, sent to him for reading, and fully approved by him, as Persia, dated 30 April 1738, of which a copy, together with the translation, we have enclosed herewith for Your Excellency's consideration. Wherefore Your Excellency's good pleasure awaiting through time, thus shall we, most esteemed, wise, prudent, and very generous lord and commanding lord, conclude this for the present herewith. We commend Your Excellency's valued persons into the sole safe keeping of the Lord of Hosts and ourselves, after humble salutation, with the utmost respect.

text_translated_detailed: Most esteemed, wise, prudent, discreet and most generous lord and commanding master. Whereas your Excellency's esteemed order contained in a letter from Persia dated 30 April 1738 by missive of 22 January of the past year, is also bringing, to learn good or bad tidings of the Wali Mahmed before Kandahar, such must be advised to your Excellency by one of the best runners, and that we cannot know whether such news might reach your Excellency sooner by way of Kerman than we have received it here, in order to be able to report such to your Excellency, it was first in compliance with that command, and secondly in order to proceed securely in such an important matter, these few humble letters, directed principally to your obedience and knowledge, that yesterday evening, by the arrival of a sapphaar [uncertain: possibly a type of messenger or courier], from Kandahar by the governor Hattembeek, the joyful tidings, over which the people were greatly moved, was received, that the Nadir Shah, favored by fortune, who is known throughout the entire world, a renowned and nearly unconquerable force, has finally and at last, twenty-eight days ago, brought to succumb under his arms, and thus from a copy of that regam [uncertain: possibly a proclamation or official document], this is appended for the brevity of the time from Persia dated 30 April 1738, being untranslated, so that unexpected news can be understood at length, to which we request ourselves to be permitted to conduct ourselves with the utmost respect, while we could not fail to express our joy over that news by having the cannons fired so that each could hear it, now wishing from our hearts that the affairs of this kingdom may take a better course, both for the welfare of the esteemed Company as for the poor exhausted subjects. "Regarding the importance of the matter" we have deemed it necessary under hope of your Excellency's favorable understanding

A hand scale is needed whereby the pound and smaller weights can also be weighed with its proper weight. Item: 18 fathoms of tarred rope of 48 threads for 4 new strands for the scale, 1 tarred line of 9 threads for bindings, and 1 strand of marline to rig the end, together with a lime mixture to prevent white ants, as well as a ration of rice or license for its purchase, as the same has not been received with the wine ration. Furthermore, the incoming cargo consists of the following: 4234 maneh of copper peisas, 14128 pounds of old copper works, and from Persia under date 30 April 1738: 25 matticaals of saffron, amounting according to invoice to ƒ 9889:7:4, wishing from the bottom of the heart that the Kieltje [ship name] may thereby obtain a speedy and safe voyage under God's guidance.

Prevention of white ants, as well as a ration of rice or license for its purchase, as the same has not been received with the wine ration. Furthermore, the incoming cargo consists of the following: 4234 maneh of copper peisas, 14128 pounds of old copper works, and from Persia under date 30 April 1738: 25 matticaals of saffron, amounting according to invoice to ƒ 9889:7:4, wishing from the bottom of the heart that the Kieltje may thereby obtain a speedy and safe voyage under God's guidance. And it further serves as notice that I have informed the chief steersman Jan Martensz of a certain rumor that has been divulged here for some days, that certain Arabs from the direction of Bassoura [Basra] would be making the beaches thereabouts unsafe. text_translated_detailed: being insufficient, it was accepted, so it was made known to you as a useful change in case such had not yet occurred before the arrival of this letter, especially since recently the Esteemed and Honorable Lord Julius Valente in Stein von Gollonesse, Commander of the Coast Malabar, after having it sent back, has sent 3 sealed letters, one for the fatherland and the other for Jerusalem and Nineveh, with the request that you allow these to participate in a good delivery at the first opportunity, in such a way that you will become further aware through the copy enclosed herewith, and since no time must be lost in this regard, and moreover as opportunity presents itself for cost, in order to correspond with the minister at Bassoura, these packets are hereby sent to you for further good care, and we shall await the answer from Persia dated 30 April 1738 with the detailed report from you. We are in great longing to know how matters stand at the aforementioned place Bassoura regarding the contagious disease, since from your last missive, apart from what was learned from the letters from Sechanse of 21 March, it appeared that it had changed somewhat for the better, nothing has been heard from the English gentlemen or anyone else, hoping therefore that in the short term we may learn that the misery has ceased and that all will have turned for the better again, with which, after wishing God's blessing upon you, we remain with friendly greetings, your devoted friends. Signed: Colonel Koenad A. Van Suchtelen, H. Jansz. van Bercheyck, S. Clement, M. Van der Crap, and P. Secretaries, P. Legrand, L. de Vries. In the margin: Gamron, 13 April 1738. text_translated_detailed: Hadje Alie from Siammael returns again to the place and confirms the news from the day before yesterday regarding the Serdar's departure. On the 18th, 19th, 20th, during these days nothing worthy of note occurred except that I found myself in poor health. On the 21st, on the 22nd, today Sjeeg Maskoor departs from here to a place approximately 8 miles from here. From Persia under date 30 April 1738. From the 24th of March, on the 25th, still on the 26th, 27th, today Sjeeg Maskoer returns again to Laco. On the 28th, still on the 29th, 30th, today toward evening there arrives unexpectedly with a Danish vessel here at the roadstead the ship the Bouche with the Company's merchants. I received the Company's letters and further papers from the hands of the aforementioned chief steersman Jan Martensz. On the 31st, Moorish feast of Abraham's offering, Sjeeg Maskoer and the Gabendhaer Aga Alie received a visit, and also received some visas from merchants, and received from the aforementioned a present of sugar cake. At home, on the 1st of April, we began to unload the vessel the Bouche and spoke with the merchants about the goods brought. We were busy unloading the Company's goods from the hold. On the 4th through the 10th, from Persia under date 30 April 1738, we were busy unloading the Bouche and speaking with the merchants. On the 5th of April, unloading the Bouche and speaking with the merchants. On the 6th, the last cargo of the Bouche came to the shore. We loaded the vessel the Bouche again with copper works. The Shabendaer Hadje Alie departed from here unexpectedly to Siammael at the house of Mister Hassan Alie Beerq. We had words with Sjeeg Maskoer, but toward evening he would send me a letter for reassurance regarding the outstanding debt that he owed me. We were busy loading the vessel the Boudie and breaking and beating the old burned copper work. [Understood/agreed:] [was signed:] I.B. V.N.

text_translated_detailed: From Persia under date 30 April 1738. Report of the Inspection of His Excellency the Company's ship the Anthonia. We have found a leak of approximately 2½ feet long, which was completely open. At that time, as the ship had taken in approximately ¾ foot of water in its bow, the matters were mostly the same, difficult to dare [to address] since the rough sea and full cargo, and on the other hand, there being no pump, we did not make the bottom more difficult in order to avoid no instability or further difficulties to undergo before and before we had made a proper report thereof. However, after we had all the goods brought back to their place, as we had found them upon our arrival on board, we had the pump properly brought to bear, and found in the time of half an hour the water to increase from 7 decimeters [modern equivalent: 7 decimeters] to 10½ decimeters [modern equivalent: 10½ decimeters], so that the leakage seemed to be found thereby. Geringe Consideratien op het bassouras Rendement vant boekjaar 173¾ ter speculatie gecompetteert als Eerstelijk vald te remanqueeren, dat de vergelijkenisse tuschen het gamronse nette rendement van 173 5/6 :'t gunt het Jongste 't zij dat w' hier aan handen hebben:/ en het bassourasse 173 3/4 in den eerste opslaag een considerabel verschil ten nadeelen van het laatse soude demonstreeren alschoon het dog in der daad gandsch Contrrire te considereeren zij, want ieder post voor post der verkogte specerijen, ande ponden stuk goederen, tegens malkanderen werdende geconfrondeert so zal men bevinden, dat Bassoura het grootste gedeelde omtrent verkoopsprijsen en behaal der arctos C„to gamron verre komt te overtreffen en waer heel weijnige ontwaeren daar gamron dien van bassoura surmanteert Ten tweede valdaan te merken dat Gamron bij gecitieerde, rendement alleen op d' aldaar verkagte specerijen bij na zo veel als wij op onsen geheelen Jaarschen om zet van alle de goederen in't generaal aan Capitaal heeft overgewonnen 't gunt Considerabel tot de groot makinge der generale pr C„to moet Contribueeren Van Persia onder dato 30 April 1738. text_translated_detailed: „ - 7814 8 6 1 2 26 28 49 /5 265 —„ 76½ 60 „ l — 121¾ - dart afvoor tsels 305: 17. — . ƒ 41 Rest dewinst „ 4:9: 10264 23/8 — 12 2/5 sch„s 98 27402 178 21176 - 1929 588435 8 53 1/8 d=m stond:/ accordeerd :/ was getek:t/ A=m V=n suchtelen /:lager:/ accordeert:/ 7m 189 /9 48 9 8 Nd 29 162 2/5137 2/5 „ From Persia, dated 30 April 1738. Minor Observations on the Bassoura Revenue for the Accounting Year 173¾, compiled for consideration. First, it should be remarked that the comparison between the net revenue of Gamron from 173 5/6 (which is the most recent one we have at hand) and the Bassoura revenue of 173 3/4 would demonstrate a considerable difference to the disadvantage of the latter in the first calculation, although in reality it should be considered quite the contrary. For when each item of the sold spices and the pound goods are compared against one another, one will find that Bassoura far surpasses Gamron in terms of selling prices and the achievement of the cost price to Gamron, and there are very few instances where Gamron exceeds that of Bassoura. Second, it should be noted that Gamron, according to the cited revenue, achieved on the spices sold there alone nearly as much capital gain as we did on our entire annual turnover of all goods in general, which must contribute considerably to the increase of the general profit percentage to Gamron. From Persia, dated 30 April 1738. Third, regarding the spices in particular, one finds that the Bassoura spices far surpass those of Gamron. Fourth, the same applies to the further pound goods this year, which would have been the case, had they not been calculated much higher than

text_translated_detailed: Having received the commission, the undersigned as expressly appointed officials from the Judicial Council, together with the aforesaid Fiscal of this directorate Simon Clement, proceeded on board the ship Opperdoes [ship name] lying here at anchor in the roadstead, for the purpose of inspecting it before its return voyage to Batavia over the route via Coromandel [Corijn]; having mustered the crew of the same according to custom, and having inspected it to the best of our ability, we found therein no private goods, and the keel measuring 15¼ feet with its forward section and 17¾ feet with its stern section drawing deep; thus hoping that we have fulfilled our duty, we remain with the required respect: humbly: Your Excellencies' obedient, compliant and dutifully obligated servants. In the margin: Gammon, the 8th of June 1738. Undersigned: was signed: F[rancis] de Wilt and J[acob] Carelsz. Further below: P[eter] Clement. We the undersigned declare that we have thoroughly compared the foregoing letters and attachments against their original and found them to be in accordance therewith. Batavia in the Castle, the 31st of January 1739. G[erard] Metske, C[ornelis] Oostwalt, D[irk] Vandkoon.
